background: Amazon Locker is a self-service delivery or pickup location where customers can pick up packages and drop off returns. Some packages are sent with standard shipping speed (3- to 5-day shipping), while other packages are sent with speed shipping (1- to 2-day shipping). The number of days a package will spend in the locker (package dwell time) is generally unknown. We want to decide how many packages to reserve for different ship options to increase the locker throughput.
constraints: Locker capacity is not violated in any period of the planning horizon
For any period of the planning horizon, the number of packages of any ship option accepted for delivery is less than or equal to demand for that ship option
Define the relationship between the number of packages accepted for delivery and the number of slots reserved for the ship option
The decision variables are constrained to be nonnegative by constraints
objective: Maximize the throughput - the total number of packages delivered to the locker in the time horizon
description: The optimization problem is focused on maximizing the throughput of packages in the lockers from all ship options \param{ShipOptions} and for \param{PlanningHorizon} days in the planning horizon. There can never be more than \param{LockerCapacity} packages in the lockers at any time. All packages are collected within 7 days. There are \param{ShipOptions} different shipment options. There are already packages \param{PackagesInLockerDayZero_{s,v}} in the locker from shipment option s and received at the locker on day v, which includes the days leading up to the current day. \param{DwellTimeProb_{s,v,t} is the dwell time probability for shipment option s on day v being present in the locker on day t. \param{Demand_{s,t}} is the demand for shipment option s on day t. \param{PackagesInLockerDayZero} is the number of packages of ship option $s$ delivered to locker on day $v$ and present in the locker at the end of day 0.
